items.title: There's a surprising message from inside Iran after the ceasefire
items.description: While the bombs may have stopped inside Iran for now, Iranians who've been speaking with ABC News say the mood on the ground is anything but happy.

items.title: Live: US to blockade Strait of Hormuz after failed peace talks
items.description: In his first comments since negotiations between the US and Iran ended with no agreed terms, US President Donald Trump says the US Navy will begin destroying mines and intercepting ships in the critical trade waters. Follow live.

items.title: Saudi Arabia gets more oil flowing as US blocks Strait of Hormuz. What you need to know about Iran today
items.description: Donald Trump knows a US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will not increase fuel supply or bring down oil prices — but will it advance peace talks?

items.title: Trump says US blockade of Strait of Hormuz to be similar to Venezuela
items.description: US President Donald Trump made the comments after the US and Iran failed to reach an agreement after 21 hours in talks in Islamabad.

items.title: 'She just lost every coin flip': How a short hike went so wrong for Celine Cremer
items.description: Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer was on the trip of a lifetime, but on a hike in Tasmania she left the trail and was never seen again. It took a private investigator, a YouTuber, loved ones and an army of volunteers to find answers.

items.title: Canada has flipped the script on childcare. Could Australia copy?
items.description: Australia definitely won't nationalise childcare, even though the data suggests there's a strong case. Perhaps a more feasible idea would be to copy what Canada has done.

items.title: Fuel crisis sees some some delaying retirement and working from home
items.description: The COVID-19 pandemic brought job losses, working from home and economic instability. Some fear the US-Israel war on Iran, which has seen fuel prices spike, has created a similar struggles.

items.title: 'Like a flea on an elephant's back': The unexpected rise of solar power
items.description: Solar power is forecast to overtake coal as the world's biggest source of electricity next year, and its growth shows no signs of slowing down. Behind its success is a little-known Australian inventor.

items.title: Bravery awards for heroes 'who stood strong' during Bondi mass stabbing
items.description: Two years on from the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbing attack, eight heroes have been recognised in a special Australian Bravery Decorations honours list.

items.title: Scientists warn of astronomy brain drain after telescope deal is axed
items.description: The Artemis II mission used space technology developed in Australia, but experts fear the axing of a multimillion-dollar telescope partnership may stifle innovation and astronomy.

items.title: The 'extraordinary' rise of Kim Jong Un's mysterious teenage daughter
items.description: North Korea leader Kim Jong Un's 13-year-old daughter is tipped to be next in line. So who is Kim Ju Ae?

items.title: Breaking: Victor Orbán concedes defeat in Hungary election
items.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has conceded defeat in the country's election.

items.title: Live: Perennial runner-up surges into Masters lead as McIlroy and Day stumble
items.description: Early double bogeys cost Jason Day and Rory McIlroy, hunting a second straight Masters victory, cost them as three-time runner-up Justin Rose streaks to the top of the leaderboard in the final round at Augusta. Follow live.

items.title: Quiz: Jump in, we're going back in time
items.description: Which state had Australia's only communist MP? And where did the Titanic sink?

items.title: How to make your workplace dog-friendly
items.description: How can employers design dog-friendly workplaces if they want to, and what does the law say about animals at work?

items.title: The recycling project turning used tennis balls into shoes
items.description: What should be done with all those used tennis balls that get inevitably sent to landfill? Lilian Xu might have found the answer.

items.title: Queen Mary of Denmark's father dies in Tasmania aged 84
items.description: The Australian-born Queen of Denmark last visited her father Professor John Donaldson during a royal visit to Tasmania last month.

items.title: Key takeaways from the Islamabad peace talks between US and Iran
items.description: After an absolute marathon of overnight negotiations and historic high-level talks between the United States and Iran, a deal to end the war that has thrown the Middle East and global energy supplies into chaos has not been reached.

items.title: Secret documents reveal landmark housing project's budget headache
items.description: Internal documents the Victorian government tried to withhold reveal that a landmark social housing construction project was facing a significant budget blowout two years after it was unveiled.

items.title: 'Where heritage meets heartbeat': Wilderness railway facing uncertain future
items.description: The West Coast Wilderness Railway in Tasmania is a beloved attraction and an important employer. The state government says it wants the railway to have a sustainable future, but hasn't said how that could be achieved.

items.title: Caretaker files for possession of impressionist Frederick McCubbin's former country home
items.description: A court has heard claims the former home of an Australian impressionist is not safe to walk through, with "black mould, evidence of vermin and wheelie bins collecting rainwater".

items.title: Love story: 'It's not my kidney now, it's yours. I'm just holding it for you'
items.description: Despite a 10-year age gap and geographical separation, Sajarn and Codey Stow have retained a close bond since childhood. That bond has only strengthened since Codey received a donor kidney from his brother last November.

items.title: The reality of living without a car in Brisbane
items.description: As the cost of owning a car goes up, some Brisbane residents are choosing to live without one. But going car-free isn't possible for everyone.

items.title: This viral craze is leaving a trail of battered bodies. Exponents want sporting legitimacy
items.description: Vali stands atop a cliff. He screams, psyching himself up. Three, two, one jump — then in mere seconds he smacks the water 42 metres below, sustaining massive injuries.

items.title: An Aussie rugby win at home is one thing but victory in NZ is another
items.description: Australian teams will only boost their chances of achieving the ultimate success in Super Rugby Pacific if they conquer the challenge of beating their New Zealand opponents across the Tasman.
